Funding ties to RHTP transformation objectives and CDC strategies for equity in diabetes and chronic disease. data.title: DE - 2025 - Delaware RHT Plan: Strategy, Initiatives, and Performance Objectives
data.highlights:
Delaware's RHTP tackles severe rural health disparities and workforce shortage by establishing new Hope Centers, deploying mobile health units, and expanding school-based health centers in Sussex and Kent Counties. The plan is backed by unified legislative and provider support, prioritizes technological innovation, value-based care, and robust data tracking, and includes concrete policy commitments to reform certificate of need, scope of practice, and telehealth reimbursement. Target outcomes include reductions in ED visits, expanded preventive care, increased rural provider access, and improved chronic disease management. These barriers disproportionately affect children and adolescents, particularly those from low- income households and underserved communities, and contribute to gaps in physical health, behavioral health, and academic outcomes. School-Based Health Centers (SBHCs) are an evidence-based strategy for addressing these access challenges by delivering comprehensive health services directly within the school setting. SBHCs have been associated with improved access to primary and preventive care, enhanced behavioral health support, reduced school absenteeism, and improved educational outcomes. The administration is also promoting multi-payer value-based care with Rural Health Transformation Program funds to bend the cost curve. These measures are designed to make care more affordable, accessible, and protective for all Delawareans.

data.highlights:

The plan supports innovations in workforce development, value-based care, and health IT infrastructure to improve rural healthcare delivery.
